today.critic_reason: A claimed annual Sharpe of 0.6 over 12 years of fresh data implies a maximum t-statistic of approximately 0.6 * sqrt(12) ≈ 2.07, which is below the bar of 3.000. The evidence (12 years of data) cannot support the claim that this strategy can pass the bar, as a net Sharpe below about 1 cannot reach a bar near 3 with this amount of data.
today.data_source: em-fx-daily daily OHLC for EM FX pairs; debt-service dates and amounts from central bank and IMF public debt calendars
today.mechanism: Emerging-market sovereigns and quasi-sovereign issuers must service USD-denominated debt on fixed contractual dates. They acquire USD by selling local currency, creating predictable, price-insensitive demand for USD around debt-service dates. This persists because debt service is a legal obligation and full currency hedging is costly or politically undesirable. The flow is macro/policy-driven (sovereign debt contracts) and forced (non-discretionary), so counterparties trading against it are not motivated by profit.
today.needs_short_or_leverage: Yes: the rule sells EM currencies against USD (short the EM currency leg) and uses leverage to equal-weight 12 pairs as one book.
today.rule: For each of 12 EM FX pairs versus USD, maintain a calendar of sovereign USD debt-service dates (bond principal/coupon and IMF repayments) published by central banks or the IMF. At the close on the second trading day before each debt-service date, take the position that buys USD and sells the EM currency (long USD/XXX or short XXX/USD as quoted). Exit at the close on the fifth trading day after entry. Include only debt-service dates where the trailing 4-quarter rolling USD debt-service amount for that currency is above its own 25th percentile. Equal-weight across pairs as one book. No look-ahead: all debt-service dates and amounts are known from public calendars before the entry date.
today.title: EM FX quarterly sovereign USD debt-service pressure
today.why: A claimed annual Sharpe of 0.6 over 12 years of fresh data implies a maximum t-statistic of approximately 0.6 * sqrt(12) ≈ 2.07, which is below the bar of 3.000. The evidence (12 years of data) cannot support the claim that this strategy can pass the bar, as a net Sharpe below about 1 cannot reach a bar near 3 with this amount of data.
today.why_new: em-fx-daily has zero prior tests; sovereign debt-service FX pressure has not been tested in this lab; using 12 currencies as one book answers power concerns that have killed single-currency flow ideas.

today.critic_reason: A claimed annual Sharpe of 0.5 over 10 years of fresh data implies a maximum t-statistic of approximately 0.5 * sqrt(10) ≈ 1.58, far below the bar of 3.000. Monthly rules need decades of data to reach such a bar, and the evidence here cannot support the claim.
today.data_source: us-etf-broad-daily daily OHLC for broad US equity ETFs
today.mechanism: US defined-contribution retirement plans (401(k), 403(b)) collect employee contributions on payroll dates, typically monthly or semi-monthly, and target-date or index funds must deploy the cash into equities within days. This creates persistent, price-insensitive net buying pressure in broad US equity ETFs. It persists because payroll deductions are automatic and fiduciary rules require invested cash rather than cash drag. The liquidity providers are sellers who transact with non-price-sensitive buyers; the flow persists because it is mandated by payroll practice and fund prospectuses, not by alpha.
today.needs_short_or_leverage: No: long only; leverage is not required.
today.rule: At the close on the first trading day of each month, go long an equal-weight basket of broad US equity ETFs (SPY, IVV, VOO, VTI, IWM). Exit at the close on the third trading day after entry. Repeat monthly. No look-ahead: monthly payroll deployment dates are known in advance from fund prospectuses and payroll calendars.
today.title: Monthly payroll defined-contribution equity inflows
today.why: A claimed annual Sharpe of 0.5 over 10 years of fresh data implies a maximum t-statistic of approximately 0.5 * sqrt(10) ≈ 1.58, far below the bar of 3.000. Monthly rules need decades of data to reach such a bar, and the evidence here cannot support the claim.
today.why_new: us-etf-broad-daily has zero prior tests; monthly payroll auto-investment as a forced-flow mechanism has not been tested here; breadth across ETFs traded as one book provides the power a single-instrument monthly rule lacks.

today.critic_reason: A claimed annual Sharpe of 0.6 over 10 years of fresh data implies a maximum t-statistic of approximately 0.6 * sqrt(10) ≈ 1.90, which is below the bar of 3.000. Even testing across multiple index CFDs as one book does not increase the number of independent years, so the evidence cannot support the claim that this strategy can pass the bar.
today.data_source: equity-index-daily daily OHLC for index CFDs plus prior-day options open interest from exchange publications
today.evidence: Stivers & Sun documented expiration-week effects in US large caps; this proposal extends the structural delta-hedging mechanism globally across index CFDs as one book to answer the power critique.
today.mechanism: Equity index options market makers must delta-hedge into the close on expiration Friday. When aggregate open interest is concentrated at strikes away from the current index level, hedging flows push the index toward the max-pain strike. This is structural (options market-making obligations) and persists because market makers are contractually obligated to hedge and cannot opt out; the flow is mechanical, not profit-motivated. Options buyers whose strikes expire worthless due to pinning pressure are the willing losers.
today.needs_short_or_leverage: Yes: the rule can go short when the index close is above the max-pain strike, and uses leverage to equal-weight the index CFD book.
today.rule: At the close on the first trading day of the monthly options-expiration week (the week containing the third Friday), for each index CFD identify the strike with the largest combined call-plus-put open interest in the near-month expiration series, using open interest published after the prior close. If the index close is below that strike, go long the index CFD; if above, go short. Exit at the close on expiration Friday. Equal-weight across index CFDs as one book. No look-ahead: open interest is known from the prior day's publication.
today.title: Monthly options-expiration week index drift across global index CFDs
today.why: A claimed annual Sharpe of 0.6 over 10 years of fresh data implies a maximum t-statistic of approximately 0.6 * sqrt(10) ≈ 1.90, which is below the bar of 3.000. Even testing across multiple index CFDs as one book does not increase the number of independent years, so the evidence cannot support the claim that this strategy can pass the bar.
today.why_new: equity-index-daily has zero prior tests; single-instrument expiration-week ideas were dropped for lack of power, and this version answers that by testing many index CFDs as one book; the mandatory delta-hedging mechanism is structural and persists.
